sources.title: PaddleOCR v3.3.0 release, 16 October 2025
sources.evidence: Dated release announces original PaddleOCR-VL and its downloadable PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B core checkpoint. This is the first release, not the October 29 Transformers integration or a later 1.5/1.6 successor.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL technical report
sources.evidence: Authors identify the PaddlePaddle Team at Baidu. Sections 2.1.2 and 2.2.2 distinguish the vision encoder, two-layer projector and autoregressive ERNIE decoder from the separate PP-DocLayoutV2 pipeline. Table 1 reports 16,384-token training in both stages. The original recognizes text, tables, formulas and charts in 109 languages.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL model card at pinned revision
sources.evidence: Names the core PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, declares Apache 2.0, and gives four task-specific image-plus-text prompts producing generated text. Its Transformers example supports element recognition; page parsing additionally uses the surrounding pipeline. The card identifies the October 16, 2025 release. Fresh pinned card read on October 27 reconfirms the original core model's nominal 0.9B designation, separately from its 0.3B language backbone.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Dense 18-layer text decoder, hidden size 1024, intermediate size 3072, 16 query heads, two KV heads and head size 128; vocabulary 103424; untied embeddings. Vision configuration has 27 layers, width 1152 and intermediate size 4304. max_position_embeddings is 131072, while max_sequence_length is null. Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval on October 27 is JSON-identical to the current original, 1.5 and 1.6 configurations, including every layer, width, vocabulary, embedding-tying and vision setting.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL model implementation
sources.evidence: Instantiates the vision Transformer, projector, dense ERNIE decoder and separate output head. All 620 checkpoint tensor names/shapes reconcile with these declarations. Rotary frequencies and position IDs are nonpersistent buffers. The instantiated vision pooling head and packing-position embedding are learned parameters, although the recognition forward path disables pooling and uses interpolated position embeddings. There is no MoE router or expert dispatch. Fresh pinned implementation and configuration-code reads on October 27 independently reproduce the three component totals and 958,588,736 complete parameters by dimension arithmetic; no weight payload was requested.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL configuration implementation
sources.evidence: Confirms the false tie_word_embeddings setting reaches the parent configuration. No vision_use_head override is supplied, so the implementation instantiates the pooling head by default. Optional classes/default arguments were checked against the actual JSON rather than counted indiscriminately.

sources.title: Complete original PaddleOCR-VL safetensors header at pinned revision
sources.evidence: Retrieved only HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-78495: 78,488-byte JSON header, 620 BF16 tensors, 958,588,736 parameter elements. Every name and shape matches a parameter reconstructed from the pinned configuration and enabled module declarations. All offsets are contiguous, nonoverlapping and account for 1,917,177,472 tensor bytes; with header and prefix the file is 1,917,255,968 bytes. No packed quantization, scales, persistent buffers or duplicate tied matrices occur. This is the sole root weight file; PP-DocLayoutV2 is a separate model, excluded. No weight payload was downloaded.

sources.title: Original checkpoint Apache License 2.0
sources.evidence: The exact model repository distributes the Apache License, Version 2.0; the pinned card declares the same license.

sources.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 technical report, original-model comparison
sources.evidence: Tables 2 and A2 label the original PaddleOCR-VL as nominally 0.9B, separately from 1.5. Section 2.1.2 explicitly says the 1.5 VLM inherits the original PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B architecture: native-resolution vision encoder, adaptive MLP connector and ERNIE-4.5-0.3B. Section 2.2.2 describes updated training rather than compression or expert changes. The structural changes in Section 2.1.1 concern separate PP-DocLayoutV3. Appendix A reserves new seal/text-spotting capabilities for 1.5; these are not transferred to the original.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL chat template
sources.evidence: Serializes user image/text input and assistant text; no structured tool-call serialization, tool-role branch or reasoning-mode switch is implemented. These omissions do not by themselves establish that all tool calling or reasoning is impossible.

sources.title: PaddlePaddle FastDeploy guide for PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B
sources.evidence: The Context Length section explicitly states a maximum supported context of 16,384 for the original PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, and its deployment examples name PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL. This is stronger evidence of supported context than the larger positional ceiling in the generic checkpoint configuration.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL tokenizer configuration
sources.evidence: model_max_length is 131072, matching the checkpoint positional ceiling. This does not establish tested or supported 128K document recognition, given the developer deployment limit of 16,384.

sources.title: Jina OCR v1 original model-team comparison, September 17, 2026
sources.evidence: Tables 1 and 2 explicitly list the exact PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 comparator at 0.9 billion total and 0.9 billion active parameters. Both tables agree on this model. This supplies Jina's nominal comparison convention, not a PaddlePaddle active disclosure or a measured count for each image-encoding/decoding phase. Five bounded searches for original PaddleOCR-VL total, active and activated counts, including developer-domain searches, found no stronger direct original-model active statement.

sources.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 developer architecture and deployment documentation
sources.evidence: Section 4 explicitly states 1.6 and 1.5 use exactly the same architecture. Sections 1-2 retain the 0.9B designation and describe loading 1.5 weights followed by continued pretraining, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. No pruning, distillation, expert expansion or new VLM component is described.

sources.title: Original PaddleOCR-VL current developer configuration, October 27 recheck
sources.evidence: Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval; parsed JSON is identical to pinned original revision 7fa00a8c55b735ba51ba49a9058f3f9c57a99a11 and the current 1.5/1.6 configurations. Corroborates unchanged VLM dimensions and nominal architecture; no weights downloaded.

sources.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 developer configuration, October 27 recheck
sources.evidence: Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval; entire parsed JSON matches the original and 1.6 configurations, including 18 text layers, width 1024, intermediate 3072, vocabulary 103424, untied embeddings, and 27 vision layers with width 1152/intermediate 4304. This corroborates the developer's explicit inherited architecture.

sources.title: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 developer configuration, October 27 recheck
sources.evidence: Fresh HTTP 200 retrieval; entire parsed JSON matches both original and 1.5 configurations. Confirms the same dense language/vision dimensions, projector inputs, vocabulary and untied embeddings behind the developer's same-architecture statement. Configuration agreement supports nominal lineage, not literal active counts by phase.

name.note: Official spelling of the original release; its core checkpoint is also named PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B. Not the later 1.5 or 1.6.

developer.note: Retain the developer label; the paper identifies PaddlePaddle Team, Baidu Inc.

family.note: The original is the V1 member of the developer-documented PaddleOCR-VL series, not the ERNIE text backbone alone.

release_date.note: Explicit original release date, also consistent with the first technical report. Later inference-backend support is not a new model release.

open_weights.note: Developer publishes the complete downloadable checkpoint under its official repository; header was accessed at a fixed revision.

license.note: Exact checkpoint license, not inferred solely from the larger PaddleOCR code repository.

parameters_b.note: Retain the complete 0.958588736B checkpoint total from the prior 620-tensor reconciliation. Fresh pinned configuration and implementation reads independently reproduce language decoder plus untied input/output embeddings 466,654,208, vision model 465,974,336, and projector 25,960,192. Vision includes the stored 37,748,736 packing-position embedding and 15,238,352 pooling head bypassed in normal recognition. The developer's 0.9B designation is nominal; the 0.3B backbone label and separate PP-DocLayoutV2 are not complete VLM counts.

active_parameters_b.note: Infer nominal 0.9B active under Jina AI/Elastic's published comparison convention: its Tables 1 and 2 explicitly give PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 0.9B active. PaddlePaddle documents identical 1.6/1.5 architecture, and the 1.5 paper explicitly inherits the original VLM architecture. Fresh original, 1.5 and 1.6 configurations are entirely identical. The changed PP-DocLayoutV3 is a separate pipeline detector. This is a labeled architecture-lineage inference of Jina's nominal convention, not a separate PaddlePaddle active disclosure, dense-equals-total arithmetic, or an exact per-token/phase tensor census. Embedding and visual-phase accounting remain unspecified.

architecture.note: Dense multimodal Transformer: NaViT-style vision encoder, two-layer MLP projector, and autoregressive ERNIE decoder with grouped-query attention and gated dense MLPs. No expert routing. The separate layout detector is not part of this VLM architecture.

context_window.note: Correct to the developer-documented supported context of 16,384, also the training sequence length. The checkpoint/tokenizer specify a 131,072 positional/tokenizer ceiling, but that is not evidence of supported 128K recognition. This conflict is recorded rather than silently treating the ceiling as the effective context.

modalities.note: The exact model consumes an image with a task prompt and generates text. PDF-to-image conversion, JSON/Markdown export and page layout are surrounding pipeline functions. Generic video token fields in config do not verify original model video support.

reasoning.note: Original documentation describes direct recognition tasks and no dedicated reasoning feature. Neither that specialization nor an absent reasoning switch verifies the baseline blanket false; clear to null. No successor training claims are transferred.

tool_call.note: The supplied template has no native structured tool-call path, and the documented tasks do not establish tool use. Absence of an advertised capability is not an explicit model-wide unsupported guarantee; clear the unsupported baseline false to null. An OpenAI-compatible serving endpoint alone does not establish tool calling.

description.value: Vision-language model from PaddlePaddle for recognizing text, tables, formulas and charts in document images, supporting 109 languages.
description.note: Describes the original VLM and its documented tasks without benchmark superlatives or capabilities introduced by successors.

patch.notes: Original PaddleOCR-VL: 0.958588736B complete checkpoint parameters, nominally 0.9B. Active 0.9B is inferred from Jina AI/Elastic's nominal 1.6 comparison convention through PaddlePaddle's documented unchanged VLM architecture across original, 1.5 and 1.6, corroborated by identical configurations. This is not a separate PaddlePaddle active disclosure or exact per-token/phase count. Total includes stored vision pooling and packing-position parameters bypassed in normal recognition; excludes the separate layout detector. Supported context is 16,384; the 131,072 config/tokenizer value is a larger ceiling. Dedicated reasoning and native tool calling remain unverified.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the exact 0.958588736B total after independently reproducing all component counts from fresh pinned code/configuration. Adds nominal 0.9B active as an explicitly attributed inference of Jina AI/Elastic's PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 comparison convention: original developer sources establish unchanged VLM architecture through 1.5 and 1.6, and all freshly fetched configurations are identical. Bounded total/active searches found no direct original-model active disclosure; phase and embedding accounting remain unspecified. Preserved all twelve other field assessments and the exact component breakdown.
